previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for persistent cough and malaise. He had been treated outpatient for presumed pneumonia with amoxicillin, prednisone, and azithromycin without improvement, followed by a brief course of levofloxacin. Admission chest X-ray revealed a right middle lobe infiltrate consistent with pneumonia. He was started on intravenous vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to ceftriaxone and levofloxacin. His hyponatremia (Na 127) was attributed to hypovolemia, improved with fluid resuscitation, and his home diuretics were held. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. His diabetes was managed with insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He remained stable, with resolving symptoms, and was discharged on oral levofloxacin to complete a 7-day course, with instructions to follow up on sodium levels and repeat chest imaging.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multifocal HCC, hx TACE x 5, RFA x 2. Latest
CT scan reviewed in ___, area of recurrence at previous TACE site in seg 8.
RFA advised. To be seen by ___ at Liver ___ on ___  // please perform RFA
to recurrence at previously TACE'd site.  Also for therapeutic paracentesis
given increasing discomfort from ascites re-accumulation

COMPARISON:   CT scan from ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ fellow and Dr. ___
radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and reviewed and agree with the trainee's
findings.
ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia was administered by the anesthesiology
department.
MEDICATIONS:  For full details please refer to anesthesiology notes.
CONTRAST: 210 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  This study involved 8 CT acquisition phases with
dose indices as follows:
   1) CT Localizer Radiograph
   2) CT Localizer Radiograph
   3) Spiral Acquisition 8.9 s, 27.2 cm; CTDIvol = 10.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 269.5
mGy-cm.
   4) Spiral Acquisition 8.9 s, 27.2 cm; CTDIvol = 8.2 mGy (Body) DLP = 213.1
mGy-cm.
   5) Spiral Acquisition 9.1 s, 27.8 cm; CTDIvol = 10.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 266.4
mGy-cm.
   6) Spiral Acquisition 9.1 s, 27.8 cm; CTDIvol = 7.9 mGy (Body) DLP = 210.3
mGy-cm.
   7) Spiral Acquisition 9.5 s, 29.2 cm; CTDIvol = 10.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 279.6
mGy-cm.
   8) Spiral Acquisition 9.5 s, 29.2 cm; CTDIvol = 10.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 280.8
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,530 mGy-cm.

PROCEDURE:  CT/US-guided RF ablation of two tumors
US-guided paracentesis

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
Following scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

A total of 2 lesions were targeted during this procedure.  The first was in
segment 8, the second was in segment 5.

Under ultrasound, a cool tip cluster radiofrequency ablation probe (15 cm long
/2.5 cm active) was advanced through the intercostal space until the tip of
the probe was just beyond the expected location of the segment 8 liver lesion.
Radiofrequency
ablation was performed at 2 different sites for a total of 12 minutes at each
site achieving a temperature of 75 degrees Celsius.

At this point, a 5 ___ ___ catheter was introduced into a pocket of
perihepatic ascites.  A total of 5 L of ascites was drained.  During the
drainage, the cluster radiofrequency probe was slowly removed, bleeding the
tract and liver capsule.  Small amount of blood tinged ascites was withdrawn
after the removal of the probe.  By the fifth bottle of ascites, the fluid was
no longer blood tinged.

Under ultrasound, a cool tip cluster radiofrequency ablation probe (15 cm long
/ 2.5 cm active ) was advanced through the intercostal space until the tip of
the probe was just beyond the expected location of the segment 5 liver lesion.
Radiofrequency ablation was performed at 2 different sites for a total of 12
minutes at each site achieving a temperature of 75 degrees Celsius.

Contrast enhanced multiphase computed tomography was obtained.  The skin was
then cleaned and a dry sterile dressing was applied. The patient was awakened
from general anesthesia without incident and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications. The patient was transferred to the
post-anesthesia care unit for further monitoring.

FINDINGS: 

Radiofrequency ablation of multifocal liver lesions, segment 8 and segment 5. 
Drainage of 5L of ascites.

IMPRESSION: 

Uncomplicated 2 site RFA, along with paracentesis (total of 5 L). Close
attention should be paid to the anterior margin of the Segment V ablation site
on follow-up imaging to assess for any residual tumor.
